la:noun:limen.gloss: threshold, doorstep, sill (bottom-most part of a doorway)
senses: threshold, doorstep, sill (bottom-most part of a doorway)
la:noun:limen.html:
līmen, ĭnis, n.
Gr. λέχρις, λοξός; Lat. obliquus, līmus; hence prop. a cross-piece
,
a threshold; the head-piece or foot-piece of a doorway, the lintel or the sill (limen superum et inferum).
Lit.: limen superum inferumque, salve,: limen superum, quod mihi misero saepe confregit caput: Inferum autem, ubi ego omnis digitos defregi meos, Novius ap. : sensim super attolle limen pedes, nova nupta,: imponere foribus,: ad limen consulis adesse,: curiae,: primo limine,at the outer threshold,.—Plur. (poet.): haec limina, intra quae puer est,; .—The moment of touching the threshold was regarded as ominous: ter limen tetigi,.—Prov.: salutare a limine, to greet in passing, i. e. to touch upon slightly, not go deeply into, .—
Transf.
A door, entrance: ubi hanc ego tetulero intra limen,: intrare intra limen,: intra limen cohibere se,to keep within doors,: marmoreo stridens in limine cardo,; : fores in liminibus profanarum aedium januae nominantur,: ad valvas se templi limenque convertisse,: penetrare aulas et limina regum,the courts and doors,: ipso in limine portae,; cf.: tremuitque saepe limite in primo sonipes,: famuli ad limina,doorkeepers, porters,: in limine portūs,at the very entrance of the haven,: densos per limina tende corymbos,.—
Still more gen., a house, dwelling, abode: matronae nulla auctoritate virorum contineri limine poterant,in the house, at home,: ad limen consulis adesse, etc.,: limine pelli,.—
Poet., the barrier in a race-course: limen relinquunt,.—
Trop., both entrance and exit.
A beginning, commencement (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): leti limine in ipso,: in limine belli,: in ipso statim limine obstare,: in limine victoriae,; ; : a limine ipso mortis revocatus,; ; .—
An end, termination (post-class.): in ipso finitae lucis limine,; cf.: limina sicut in domibus finem quendam faciunt, sic et imperii finem limen esse veteres voluerunt,.

la:adj:limosus.html:
līmōsus, a, um, adj.
2. limus
,
full of mud or slime, slimy, miry, muddy: quae (aqua) flumine Nilo fertur, adeo est limosa atque turbida, etc.,: limosoque palus obducit pascua junco,i. e. growing in muddy places,; cf. radix,: lacus,: ripae,: harena,.—Plur. absol.: līmōsa, ōrum, n., muddy or miry places, .

la:noun:limes.gloss: a limit set between two estates or fields, border, boundary
senses: a limit set between two estates or fields, border, boundary
a fortified boundary line, a boundary wall
la:noun:limes.html:
līmĕs, ĭtis, m.
root in līmus; cf. limen, and Gr. λέχρις; cf.
,
a cross-path, balk between fields.
Lit., the Romans usually had in their fields two broad and two narrower paths; the principal balk from east to west was called limes decumanus; that from north to south was called cardo; of the two smaller ones, that running from east to west was called prorus, the other, from north to south, transversus, and 34; : lutosi limites,. —
Transf. (mostly poet.).
A boundary, limit between two fields or estates, consisting of a stone or a balk: partiri limite campum,: saxum antiquum, ingens, campo quod forte jacebat, Limes agro positus, litem ut discerneret arvis,: effodit medio de limite saxum,.—
A fortified boundaryline, a boundary-wall: cuncta inter castellum Alisonem ac Rhenum novis limitibus aggeribusque permunita,: limite acto promotisque praesidiis,: penetrat interius, aperit limites, .—
In gen., any path, passage, road, way; also, by-street, by-road: eo limite Athenienses signa extulerunt,: profectus inde transversis limitibus,: lato te limite ducam,: acclivis,: limite recto fugere,: transversi,by-roads, Fabr.; 31, 39, 5; 41, 14 init.: limes Appiae, the line of the Appian street (for the street itself), : limite acto (i. e. facto),.— Of the channel of a stream: solito dum flumina currant Limite,; .—Of the track of light left behind them by comets, fiery meteors, torches, etc.: flammiferumque trahens spatioso limite crinem, Stella micat,: tum longo limite sulcus Dat lucem,; : sectus in obliquo est lato curvamine limes,the zodiac,: latum per agmen Ardens limitem agit ferro,; cf. ; ; .—
A line or vein in a precious stone: nigram materiam distinguente limite albo,.—
Trop.
A boundary, limit: limes carminis,: aestuat infelix angusto limite mundi,.—
A distinction, difference: judicium brevi limite falle tuum,: quaedam perquam tenui limite dividuntur,.—
A way, path: si maledicitis vostro gradiar limite,: bene meritis de patria quasi limes ad caeli aditum patet,; : eundem limitem agere,to go the same way, employ the same means,.

la:noun:limbus.html:
limbus, i, m.,
a border that surrounds any thing, a hem, welt, edge, selvage, fringe; a belt, band, girdle.
Lit.: Sidoniam picto chlamydem circumdata limbo,; (this the better read., others nimbo): indutus chlamydem Tyriam, quam limbus obibat Aureus,; ; 2, 734; : frontem limbo velata pudicam,with a headband, fillet,; cf.: imminuerent frontes limbis,: picto discingit pectora limbo, with a girdle,

belt, .—

Transf. *
The zodiac: extra limbum XII. signorum,; id. ap. Prob. ad .—
A noose, snare, for catching animals, .

la:verb:limo.html:
līmo, āvi, ātum (arch. limassis, for limaveris, ), 1, v. a.
lima
,
to file.
Lit.: gemmis scalpendis atque limandis,.—
Transf.
To file off: plumbum limatum,lead-filings,: limata scobs,: cornum limatum lima lignaria,: acumen ossis,.—
To rub, whet: cornu ad saxa limato,; hence, limare caput cum aliquo,to kiss,; .—
Trop.
In gen., to file, polish, finish: quaedam institui, quae limantur a me politius,: stilus hoc maxime ornat ac limat,: ut ars aliquid limare non possit,: vir nostrorum hominum urbanitate limatus,.—
In partic.
To investigate accurately, to clear of every thing superfluous: veritas ipsa limatur in disputatione,: subtiliter mendacium,. —
Cum se ipse consulto ad minutarum causarum genera limaverit, has prepared one's self thoroughly for, .—
To file off, take away from, diminish: tantum alteri affinxit, de altero limavit,: de tua prolixa beneficaque natura limavit aliquid posterior annus,: commoda alicujus,: multum inde decoquent anni, multum ratio limabit,. —Hence, līmātus, a, um, P. a., polished, refined, elegant, fine, accurate: vir oratione maxime limatus,: jure madens, varioque togae limatus in usu,: pressum limatumque genus dicendi,; : Attici,.—Comp.: limatius dicendi genus,: comis et urbanus fuerit limatior idem,: limatius ingenium,.—Hence, adv.: līmātē, finely, elegantly, accurately; comp.: limatius scriptum,: limatius quaerere,.

la:adj:limus.html:
līmus, a, um (līmis, e, ;
v.infra), adj.
Gr. λέχριος, λέχρις, λοξός; Lat. licinus, ob-liquus, luxus
, sidelong, askew, aslant, askance.
Lit.: limis oculis aspicere,to look sideways, look askance,: limis subrisit ocellis,: (leones) nec limis intuentur oculis aspicique simili modo nolunt,: limibus oculis eos contuens,.—So, limis aspicere (sc. oculis), : limi, et ut sic dicam venerei (sc. oculi),: oculi contuitu quoque multiformes, truces et limi,: limi Di,the guardian gods of obliquities,.—
Transf., of persons, looking sideways: neque post respiciens, neque ante prospiciens, sed limus intra limites culinae, Varr. ap. ; cf. .—Hence, adv.: līmō, sideways, askance: leones numquam limo vident,; for which: limis oculis in (v. the passage above).

la:noun:limus.html:
līmus, i, m.
root lib-; Gr. λείβω, to pour; cf. Lat. lino; Gr. λίμνη, λιμήν
,
slime, mud, mire.
Lit.: atque omnis mundi quasi limus in imum Confluxit gravis et subsedit funditus ut faex,: luta et limum aggerebant, ap. : frumenti acervos sedisse illitos limo,: profundo limo cum ipsis equis hausti sunt,: amnis abundans Exit et obducto late tenet omnia limo,: amnes Felicem trahunt limum,: limo Turbata aqua,: veteri craterae limus adhaesit,.—
Transf.
Excrement in the intestines, .—
Dirt, mire: limumque inducere monstrat,.—
Trop., filth, pollution, etc.: pectora sic mihi sunt limo vitiata malorum,.

la:verb:limito.html:
līmĭto, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
limes
,
to enclose within boundaries or limits, to bound.
Lit.: vineas limitari decumano XVIII. pedum latitudinis,; cf.: limitatus ager est in centurias dimensus, Paul. ex Müll.—
Trop., to fix, settle, determine: limitata est pecuaria quaestio,.
